subject: general
question: Wood's Dispatch was concerned with which of the following reforms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Education.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Wood's Dispatch, officially known as the "Wood's Dispatch on Education," was issued in **1854 by Sir Charles Wood,** the then President of the Board of Control of India.
 
• It is often considered the **foundation of modern education policy** in India.
 
• The dispatch emphasized the need for expanding education in India, particularly in the English language, and recommended the establishment of universities, colleges, and schools.
 
• It also highlighted the importance of both primary and higher education and aimed to promote women's education.
 
• The document laid the **groundwork for future educational reforms** and the development of a structured education system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Railways:**

 
 
• The introduction of railways in India was a significant British initiative during the 19th century, aimed at improving transportation and trade.
 
• The first railway line opened in **1853, connecting Bombay (now Mumbai) to Thane.**
 
• Railways played a crucial role in the economic development of India, facilitating the movement of goods and people, but also served colonial interests.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation:**
 
 
• Irrigation projects were** vital for agriculture in India**, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
• The British implemented various irrigation schemes to enhance agricultural productivity, which in turn **supported the export of cash crops.**
 
 
 
• **Industry:**
 
 
• Industrial development in India was **limited under British rule**, with a focus on raw material extraction for British industries.
 
• The late 19th and early 20th centuries saw the establishment of some industries, particularly textiles and jute, but Indian entrepreneurship faced significant challenges.
